item.title: Re: Matt Morgan: What mermaids can teach us about misinformation
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The danger of mermaids as a threat to health and life through their offering of false promises was well represented in medieval church carvings (1). These signified mermaids as the embodiment of sin, posing not just a risk to life, but (to the religiously minded) a threat to the soul. item.title: Re: Families are being rehoused hundreds of miles from home—GPs raise alarm over health harms and service strain
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor A generation ago most residents wouldn't have classed their area as 'deprived' so why has Camden, amongst others, taken so little care of its residents? The kind of segregation as described by CQC is generated by wealth and advantages of background and is part of a pattern across cities and towns of UK. item.title: Re: Palantir and NHS: BMA to tell members to limit use of tech system
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Despite the scandals, the Health Minister has made no statement to inform people of the government's intentions regarding Palantir. item.title: Synthetic drug potency matters, but polysubstance unpredictability matters even more
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Guenot’s article (1) usefully anticipates a scenario that many clinicians in Europe still frame as “North America’s problem”: a rapidly evolving market in which highly potent synthetic opioids, stimulants, and sedatives appear unpredictably in heroin, counterfeit tablets, and even cannabinoid products, creating sudden clusters of collapse and an unfamiliar clinical pattern in emergency care and the community. item.title: The False Dichotomy
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Post Graduate Training Bodies sit in a central and influential space between Regulatory and Government authorities in many countries worldwide.
